**Defensible v1 for a 12‑hospital AI Sepsis‑Risk CDSS** | Domain | Key Deliverables (v1) | Why it matters | |--------|-----------------------|----------------| | **Clinical Safety** | • Retrospective validation on each hospital’s active inpatient data set (≥ 80 % of encounters, ≥ 10 k patients).
• Prospective pilot in 2–3 hospitals with a “shadow” mode that records predictions but does not alter care for the first 30 days.
• Performance metrics derived from peer‑reviewed literature and vendor reports: AUROC 0.75–0.85, sensitivity 70–80 % at a 5 % false‑positive rate (or equivalent operating point).
• Governance review of a statistically representative sample of alerts (e.g., 1 % of all alerts) and key process metrics (override rate, adverse event rate) during the pilot.
• Real‑time monitoring dashboard: alert volume, override rate, escalation events, patient outcomes (mortality, ICU LOS).
• Escalation protocol: if ≥ 10 % of alerts are overridden or lead to an adverse event within a 7‑day window, trigger a full safety review and temporary suspension. | Provides evidence that the tool performs reliably in the local data environment and can be safely integrated into workflow without creating new harms. | | **Legal & Regulatory Exposure** | • HIPAA Privacy & Security risk assessment for all data flows; remediate gaps before go‑live.
• FDA SaMD guidance review: classify the product (likely Class I or II). If it is “advisory” and does not directly alter standard of care, a 510(k) may be exempt; otherwise file a pre‑market notification with performance data, risk analysis, and labeling. Document the exemption determination.
• ISO 14971 risk management plan (optional but strengthens governance).
• Professional liability coverage review: ensure AI‑related claims are covered; obtain endorsements if needed.
• EHR CDSS documentation alignment: use existing “CDS Documentation” fields (e.g., Epic) rather than adding new consent checkboxes. Document that alerts are advisory and part of the standard workflow.
• Data governance policy: define data ownership, retention periods, third‑party access; reference HIPAA Privacy Rule and HITECH for obligations. | Protects the health system from regulatory fines, malpractice claims, and ensures patient privacy while aligning with current FDA and HIPAA guidance. | | **Financial Structure** | • Per‑seat annual subscription: $1,500–$4,000 (range based on vendor quotes and feature set).
• Cost allocation negotiated per hospital: e.g., 60 % to vendor, 40 % to hospital IT/clinical operations, reflecting infrastructure and support costs.
• ROI model built from published economic evaluations of sepsis CDSS (e.g., Sepsis Early Warning System studies). Example assumptions:
 – Baseline sepsis mortality 12 %; target post‑AI 9 % (3 pp reduction).
 – Average cost per severe sepsis case $25,000.
 – Expected savings: 30 cases × $25k = $750k per hospital annually.
 – Subscription cost: $3,000 → payback ≈ 4 months (illustrative); sensitivity analysis shows 12‑24 month payback under conservative assumptions.
• Performance‑based Service Level Agreement (SLA): minimum alert accuracy and uptime; penalties for sustained degradation rather than fee adjustments.
• Quality‑metric mapping: document how the tool may improve bundle compliance (e.g., early lactate measurement) but do not claim automatic HEDIS credit. | Demonstrates economic value, justifies subscription fees, and aligns incentives with patient outcomes while remaining realistic about savings and payback. | --- ## Step‑by‑Step Rollout Plan 1. **Governance & Stakeholder Alignment** * Form a cross‑hospital steering committee (clinical leads, IT, legal, finance). * Draft a “Clinical AI Governance Charter” that defines roles, decision rights, escalation paths, and data‑sharing agreements. 2. **Data Readiness** * Map required EHR elements (vital signs, labs, demographics) to the vendor’s input schema. * Verify real‑time data feeds; target latency < 5 s for vital sign streams. * Conduct a HIPAA risk assessment and remediate identified gaps. 3. **Regulatory & Legal Prep** * Review FDA SaMD guidance (21 CFR 820.30) to determine classification. * If exempt, document the exemption determination; if not, prepare a 510(k) submission with retrospective validation data. * Update malpractice policies and obtain insurer endorsement for AI‑related claims. * Finalize data governance policy referencing HIPAA Privacy Rule and HITECH. 4. **Pilot Deployment** * Select 2–3 hospitals representing diverse patient populations. * Run in “shadow” mode for 30 days: capture predictions, record overrides, but do not alter care. * Collect metrics: alert volume per 1,000 encounters, override rate, adverse event rate, baseline vs. post‑pilot sepsis outcomes. 5. **Clinical Safety Review** * Steering committee reviews pilot data (sampled alerts, key metrics). * If performance meets thresholds and no safety signals emerge, approve full rollout; otherwise iterate on algorithm or alert threshold. 6. **Full Rollout & Training** * Deploy to all 12 hospitals in a phased schedule (e.g., one hospital per week). * Conduct provider training: interpretation of risk scores, documentation requirements, escalation procedures. * Update EHR order sets and care pathways to incorporate the new risk score. 7. **Ongoing Monitoring & Governance** * Real‑time dashboard for alert volume, override rates, patient outcomes. * Monthly safety reviews; quarterly financial reviews. * Annual audit of algorithm performance against updated clinical guidelines. 8. **Continuous Improvement** * Feed real‑world data into the vendor’s model retraining pipeline under strict governance. * Adjust risk thresholds as evidence evolves. * Reassess regulatory status if scope changes (e.g., adding new decision points). --- ## Quick Reference Checklist | Area | Item | Status | |------|------|--------| | **Clinical** | Retrospective validation ≥ 80 % coverage? | ✅ | | | Prospective pilot in 2 hospitals? | ☐ | | | Performance metrics meet literature range? | ☐ | | **Legal/Regulatory** | HIPAA audit passed? | ✅ | | | FDA SaMD classification & exemption determination documented? | ☐ | | | Liability coverage updated? | ☐ | | **Financial** | Subscription fee set (range $1,500–$4,000)? | ✅ | | | ROI model built with sensitivity analysis? | ☐ | | | Performance‑based SLA drafted? | ☐ | --- ## Bottom Line A defensible v1 is not a “plug‑and‑play” subscription; it is an integrated system that: * **Proves safety** through realistic retrospective validation, a controlled prospective pilot, and ongoing governance. * **Mitigates legal risk** by aligning with HIPAA, FDA SaMD guidance, and professional liability coverage. * **Demonstrates value** via a transparent financial model grounded in published evidence and performance‑based SLAs. With these elements in place, the health system can roll out the AI sepsis‑risk CDSS across all 12 hospitals while protecting patients, providers, and its own bottom line.
